extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, industry commenters, economists, and SEC staff assessing or estimating compliance costs of SEC climate-related disclosure rules
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and component-by-component cost estimation approach for the SEC's final climate-related disclosure rules (Regulation S-K and S-X amendments), including assumptions, adjustments, and example cost ranges for affected registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance cost components (governance/strategy/risk management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate costs for governance disclosure; disclosure regarding climate-related risks that have material impacts on strategy, business model, and outlook; and risk management disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page treats TCFD disclosure as a starting point for these provisions and estimates $327,000 in the first year and $183,000 annually thereafter for these disclosures. Analysis separates these components from other optional or conditionally required components (e.g., emissions measurement, targets). Where commenters provided aggregated TCFD costs, the SEC adjusts to isolate these provisions (see adjustment methodology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis reporting costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate reporting costs for registrants that conduct scenario analysis and must provide attendant disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated at $12,000 in the first year and $6,000 in subsequent years for registrants required to disclose scenario analysis. Scenario-analysis costs are treated separately because not all registrants will be required to undertake scenario analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions disclosure costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate costs for measuring and disclosing Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions where required after phase-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated compliance costs for these disclosures are $151,000 in the first year of compliance and $67,000 annually thereafter. The analysis notes that some comment submissions gave combined costs that included emissions measurement blended with other activities; adjustments were applied to isolate relevant emissions costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party assurance costs for emissions disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate costs of obtaining third-party assurance for GHG emissions disclosures (limited and reasonable assurance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated limited assurance cost is $50,000 and reasonable assurance is $150,000. The page explains phase-in timing (assurance after phase-in) and uses these estimates in upper/lower bound scenarios for registrant cost ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and goals reporting costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate costs for registrants that voluntarily establish climate-related targets or goals and must provide attendant disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated reporting costs are $10,000 in the first year of establishing a target and $5,000 in subsequent years. Separately, the analysis derives an adjustment factor for 'setting targets and goals' ($54,015) used to subtract target-related costs from aggregated TCFD estimates when isolating governance/strategy/risk management costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Regulation S-X and incremental audit fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate costs tied to compliance with the amendments to Regulation S-X and related incremental audit fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC estimates an upper bound of $500,000 in the first year and $375,000 annually thereafter for Regulation S-X amendments, and an upper bound of $23,000 for incremental audit fees. The analysis notes that actual costs will vary by registrant and may be lower due to narrowing of proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant-level compliance cost range and example scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Present illustrative low-end and high-end registrant examples and an overall range of average annual compliance costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on applicability of items, annual compliance costs (averaged over first ten years) could range from less than $197,000 to over $739,000. Example low-end registrant (only governance/strategy/risk management disclosures applies) averages $197,000/year; full-applicability example could incur $872,000 first-year and $739,000 average annual cost. Use such scenarios to reflect heterogeneity across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality-assessment cost consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that registrants may incur costs to determine whether particular disclosure items are material, even if ultimately no disclosure is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC did not provide a standalone estimate for materiality determinations because commenters did not separate those costs; instead, materiality-assessment costs are reflected to the extent they are part of TCFD-like disclosure activities captured in governance/strategy/risk management cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative estimation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a conservative approach in estimating compliance costs, erring on the side of overstating rather than understating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where assumptions were necessary, the SEC chose ones that tend to overstate costs; when converting initial to ongoing costs, they used conservative percentage reductions; sample inputs skew toward large-cap firms so conservatism helps avoid underestimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for aggregated cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenters provide aggregate TCFD or climate-related costs that include multiple components, subtract estimated component costs (e.g., targets, emissions measurement) to obtain an 'adjusted cost' for the provisions of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology subtracts two adjustment factors from aggregated TCFD ongoing costs: $54,015 for setting targets and goals and $79,236 for assessing Scope 1/2/(some Scope 3) emissions. After adjustments, the median of the adjusted costs is used for the provisions of interest (governance/strategy/risk management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external comparators to inform estimates (UK FCA and BEIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage cost estimates from existing disclosure regimes (e.g., UK's FCA 'comply-or-explain' and BEIS mandatory rule) to inform and calibrate SEC cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BEIS and FCA rules provide first-year and ongoing cost estimates for similar TCFD-aligned components (governance, strategy, risk management). The SEC converts GBP to USD and uses observed reductions from initial to ongoing costs in those rules (FCA: 56% reduction; BEIS: 32% reduction) to estimate ongoing costs when only initial costs are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of central tendency (median) and selection of data points
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply medians of adjusted cost observations to represent typical costs and to reduce influence of outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After applying adjustments to source estimates, the SEC takes the median of the resulting adjusted costs (e.g., median of Column (6) in Table 8 is $183,135). When even number of data points, the arithmetic mean of the two middle values is used. The SEC notes sample limitations (mostly large-cap inputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for source costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether a source's reported cost includes target-setting or emissions-measurement by inspecting the qualitative description; only subtract adjustment factors when the source explicitly includes those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of twelve TCFD cost estimates in Table 8, the SEC assumed three included target-related activities and five included emissions-measurement activities. When ambiguity exists, the SEC only assumes inclusion if the source qualitatively references those activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of FTE/hours to dollar costs and currency/time adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert reported FTEs, burden hours, and initial costs into dollar ongoing costs using hourly cost estimates, percent reductions from initial to ongoing, and currency exchange rates as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (3 FTEs)*(40 hrs/wk)*(36 wks)*($444/hr) = $1,918,080; GBP to USD conversion used 2022 avg exchange rate (1.2369 USD/GBP). For sources that only provide initial costs, apply median percent reductions (e.g., 44% median) to estimate ongoing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in timing and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for statutory or regulatory phase-in periods which delay certain requirements (e.g., Scope 1/2 disclosures, assurance) and therefore affect when costs are incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs are estimated by distinguishing first-year (initial compliance) costs from ongoing annual costs after applicable phase-in periods. Phase-in influences aggregate first-year versus ongoing estimates and registrant-level scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors explaining variance in compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify registrant characteristics and choices that cause large variance in costs (company size, industry, business model, corporate complexity, existing practices, internal expertise, third-party advisor usage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC emphasizes that actual costs can vary significantly across registrants and that smaller registrants likely face lower absolute costs; decisions to use external consultants vs in-house resources materially affect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions selected to bias conservatively where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When data are incomplete the analysis adopts assumptions that tend to overstate rather than understate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include assuming upper-bound initial costs when only 'less than' values are given (e.g., treat 'less than $100,000' as $100,000) and selecting percent reductions consistent with conservative estimates when converting initial to ongoing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of voluntary data and selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that most voluntary cost submissions come from large-cap firms and may not be representative of the broader set of affected registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC notes selection bias and the aggregation of multiple components in voluntary submissions making disaggregation difficult; uses adjustments and conservative steps to mitigate but still recognizes representativeness limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-element compliance cost estimation structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the overall compliance cost estimation into five specific elements to be estimated separately and then combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five elements are: (1) governance disclosure + strategy/business model/outlook + risk management disclosure; (2) assessing and disclosing Scope 1 and 2 emissions; (3) obtaining third-party assurance for GHG disclosures; (4) reporting costs of scenario analysis and targets/goals; (5) costs associated with amendments to Regulation S-X and incremental audit costs. The analysis proceeds to review each element in turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation and use of specific adjustment factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Create numeric adjustment factors for components frequently embedded in aggregated estimates (e.g., targets and emissions measurement) and apply them consistently to isolate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC derived an adjustment factor for setting targets and goals of $54,015 (median of multiple adjusted sources) and an adjustment factor for assessing Scopes 1/2/(some 3) emissions of $79,236. These are subtracted from aggregated TCFD ongoing cost reports where those components are judged to be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of initial versus ongoing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between first-year (initial) implementation costs and ongoing annual costs, and convert initial to ongoing estimates using observed percent reductions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed percent reductions from initial to ongoing in comparator rules (BEIS and FCA) were used (BEIS 32% or 23% in one place; FCA 56% or 67% in different places), and the SEC often uses the median percent reduction (e.g., 44% in examples) to estimate ongoing costs from reported initial costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multi-component aggregated reports
rubrics_metrics.description: When a commenter's reported costs cover multiple activities not all required by the final rules, isolate the subset applicable to the rule by subtracting estimated costs of non-applicable components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document gives examples where aggregated TCFD costs included measuring emissions and target-setting; the SEC subtracts median-derived estimates for those activities to obtain adjusted estimates for the provisions that align with the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of third-party service price ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Use market pricing information for third-party services (e.g., TCFD reporting, GHG accounting, target-setting) to inform cost estimates and adjustment factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: TCFD reporting excluding emissions measurement and targets ~ $100,000 average; assessing Scopes 1/2/3 $75,000–$125,000; GHG accounting fees $11,000–$105,000; target-setting $20,000–$30,000. Such ranges inform medians and adjustment calculations.
